parts:
Alastair,

I'm no expert, but I had to do something similar to this recently, and something like the plot below helped me compare several factors at once.

ggplot(m.data,aes(instance,value,colour=variable))+
geom_point(aes(shape=variable))+
geom_line(stat="summary",fun.y=median,aes(group=variable))+
facet_grid(.~option)




Adam Loveland

messages.subject: Re: Creating side by side columns in geom_point plot
parts:
How about something completely different? :)

g <- ggplot(m.data, aes(x = value, y = variable))
g + geom_point(aes(colour = option), size = 2.5) + facet_wrap(~ instance, ncol = 1) +
    theme_bw() + opts(legend.position = c(0.88, 0.88))

To reduce some of the overplotting,

g + geom_point(aes(colour = option), size = 2.5, position = position_jitter(height = 0.2)) +
    facet_wrap(~ instance, ncol = 1) +
    theme_bw() + opts(legend.position = c(0.88, 0.88))

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Creating side by side columns in geom_point plot
parts:
Hi:

Actually, there's another one I like better: (data in the original post not reproduced here)

h <- ggplot(m.data, aes(x = value, y = instance))
h + geom_point(aes(colour = option), size = 2.5, position = position_jitter(height = 0.2)) +
    facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol = 1) +
    theme_bw() + opts(legend.position = c(0.88, 0.75))

This assumes the facets represent different variables, so the comparisons among instances are evident and easy to interpret. If you have a number of variables and space is no issue, then you could make several ggplots that would take up a few pages. One way to do this is to create a new variable in your data frame whose values would map to different graphics pages, and then use successive subsets of the data to plot individual pages. The reason why it's better to have instances on the y-axis is because it's a lot easier to read the labels that way. With 20 instances, you could probably get two, maybe three faceted variables per page.

HTH,
Dennis
